question: What filesystem boundary should OpenClaw expose for this request: deny-wins `tools.fs.allowedPaths`/`denyPaths`, access-mode `tools.fs.roots`, or a narrower workspace-only policy plus a separate exec-policy split?
rationale: This defines a public config surface and local data-access boundary, and the open implementation candidates make different compatibility, operator UX, and false-security tradeoffs.

options.title: Settle one `tools.fs` path-policy contract
options.body: Choose one canonical config shape, require normalization/symlink/deny precedence coverage, and make exec coverage explicit before merging either implementation path.

options.title: Split exec into a separate tracker
options.body: Allow a file-tool-only policy only if docs and labels clearly state shell-mediated file access remains a separate security boundary.

options.title: Stay with OS/container isolation
options.body: Decline host path ACLs only if maintainers decide OpenClaw should not own filesystem path policy beyond workspaceOnly and sandbox backends.

recommendation.title: Settle one `tools.fs` path-policy contract
recommendation.body: Choose one canonical config shape, require normalization/symlink/deny precedence coverage, and make exec coverage explicit before merging either implementation path.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already framed the prior keep-open review and has the strongest current history on the config/schema and workspaceOnly security path.
